_comment: SHOSMED physics, FOURTH 60-question block. Implemented 19 November 2026 from
SHOSMED_Physics_Batch4_Review_and_Claude_Prompt.txt.
HOW THE IDS WERE VERIFIED. The review warned against assuming a
phys-181..phys-240 run or zero overlap, so the map was derived by FULL
CONTENT MATCH of each original stem plus all four original option texts
against all 280 physics records, on a canonical form that decodes named
HTML entities, strips tags, folds sub/superscripts to plain digits and
normalises dashes, Greek letters, arrows and whitespace.
- All 60 matched EXACTLY. No match was ambiguous and none needed the
explanation as a tie-break.
- Q34’s export carries an "Unanswered" line before its stem. That string
appears in NO stored field anywhere in the physics bank, so it is
interface text; it was dropped from the signature and Q34 still matched
uniquely.
- Every stored topic equalled the signature topic.
- All 60 stored answer letters equalled the review key block, and the
review changes no letter, so NO key was changed.
The block turns out to be phys-181 .. phys-240 in display order, contiguous,
but that is a RESULT of the matching rather than the assumption the review
warned against. It does not overlap the 180 ids of the three earlier blocks
(phys-1..phys-180), so all 60 are newly reviewed ids.
TWO PRESENTATION BANDS, confirmed in storage rather than assumed:
- Q1..Q45 carry one Key Concept each (45), no educational-point block and
no Bottom Line. Their distractor feedback is stored as a <ul> of three

- 180 distractor bodies in all, exactly as the review states. 83 were
replaced and 97 retained; none was added or removed.
HEADING SYNCHRONIZATION. The review asks the 56 edited items to carry an
A/B/C/D label on every feedback heading, with the heading reproducing the
item’s own option text, while the four KEEP items are exempt. In Q1..Q45
that label was added INSIDE the existing <li>, so the stored list
presentation and its section heading are preserved and only the heading text
changes. In Q46..Q60 the paragraphs already had labels and only the heading
text was re-synchronized. No stored keyed-heading style was changed: all 60
are unlettered and reproduce their keyed option.
NOTATION, inspected rather than assumed. Every one of the items the review
flags (Q7, Q23, Q24, Q27, Q30, Q31, Q37, Q39, Q41, Q42, Q46-Q53) already
stores <sup>/<sub> markup and no Unicode exponent. Q53 stores 10<sup>0</sup>
and 10<sup>-12</sup>, so the export’s "100" was a flattening artifact, not a
defect. Q46 and Q47 store the letter w for angular frequency, never a
flattened ω, so w is kept throughout as the review directs. The one real
notation defect in the block is Q41’s Key Concept, which used the UPPERCASE
Greek letters U+0391, U+0392 and U+0393 for the particle symbols; its
replacement Key Concept uses the conventional lowercase forms.
New text uses <sup>/<sub> markup with the ASCII hyphen this block stores
inside an exponent, and literal Greek characters, which render identically
to the named entities the older passages use. Retained passages keep
whatever they already store.

presentation.band_2: Q46-Q60: 48 educational points in 15 blocks, 15 Bottom Lines, no Key Concept

deviations: The four KEEP items (Q3, Q8, Q20, Q23) are exempt from the heading rule, so they alone still carry unlettered <li> lead-ins while the other 41 first-band items now carry A/B/C/D labels. The review requires exactly this ("No edits, including no heading normalization"), so the block ends mixed by design.

The A/B/C/D labels were added INSIDE the stored containers rather than converting Q1-Q45 to paragraphs. The review asks only for the labels and says not to rewrite these items to standardize headings, so the <ul> list of Q1-Q45 and the paragraphs of Q46-Q60 both stay as stored. This differs from the first three physics blocks, which use lettered paragraphs throughout.

Where a complete main block is replaced, the stored exp-diagram or centred formula container goes with it, because the review's instruction to preserve useful formula layout applies only "unless its contents are explicitly replaced". That is why 10 items lose paragraphs on balance; no table was lost, and Q1, Q4 and Q54 received their replacement tables.
notes: The review's own inventory was cross-checked and closes: 39 stems, 22 complete main blocks, 6 scoped main passages or cells, 32 Key Concepts, 4 educational-point blocks, 12 individual points, 11 Bottom Lines, 4 option texts and 83 replacement distractor bodies, leaving the four KEEP items with no listed edit at all.
All 180 distractor bodies already existed. 83 were replaced and 97 retained (85 in the edited items plus the 12 inside the four KEEP items). None was added, removed or duplicated.

No answer letter, id, topic or subject moved, and no answer-position rebalancing was done. Q4 B and Q18 B changed the keyed option, so those two keyed headings were re-synchronized; Q13 D and Q19 C are distractors and moved no key.

Q34 is the major scenario repair: in the stored directions both forces on the electron pointed downward, so the keyed equation could not make them cancel. E now points downward, B still into the page, the electron still moves right, and answer B is unchanged.

Q13 is the competing-answer repair: the stored option D, a collimating lens, is a real eyepiece function when the final image is at infinity. It was replaced rather than denied, and the explanation now says a relaxed-eye eyepiece does emit parallel rays.
'Back to Dashboard', 'Unanswered' and 'Report an issue' appear in no stored field anywhere in the physics bank, so they are interface text and were not counted as content corrections.
No CSS was changed. The approved review-option wrappers and the scoped sup/sub rule are untouched, and no bank-wide Unicode normalization was applied.
Structural and consistency checks establish scope and presentation. They do not establish scientific accuracy, which rests on the content review itself.

coverage.note: Reconciled from unique verified physics ids: this block overlaps none of the three earlier blocks (phys-1..phys-180), so coverage becomes 240 of 280. The remaining 40 physics records are outside all four blocks and untouched.
